input.prompt:
Repository: <workspace> (this is the Hono core repo).

Task: Fix a header-injection risk in `c.redirect()` in `src/context.ts`, and add regression tests in `src/context.test.ts`.

Current implementation (src/context.ts lines 768-780):
```ts
redirect = <T extends RedirectStatusCode = 302>(
  location: string | URL,
  status?: T
): Response & TypedResponse<undefined, T, 'redirect'> => {
  const locationString = String(location)
  this.header(
    'Location',
    // Multibytes should be encoded
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
    !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString) ? locationString : encodeURI(locationString)
  )
  return this.newResponse(null, status ?? 302) as any
}
```

Problem: when the location is pure 8-bit ASCII, it is passed through verbatim, so raw CR (`\r`) / LF (`\n`) reach the `Location` header and enable response splitting / header injection. Applying `encodeURI` unconditionally is NOT acceptable because it double-encodes already percent-encoded input (`encodeURI('%0D%0A') === '%250D%250A'`, `encodeURI('https://e.com/a%20b') === 'https://e.com/a%2520b'`), breaking existing valid redirects.

Required behavior:
1. Raw CR and LF characters in the location string must be percent-encoded to `%0D` and `%0A` respectively in the `Location` header (consider handling `\r\n` as a pair so it becomes `%0D%0A`; a simple regex replace of each char with its escape is fine).
2. Valid redirects must be preserved exactly: `/destination`, `https://example.com/destination`, `new URL(...)`, multibyte URLs (still `encodeURI`-encoded as today), and already percent-encoded inputs such as `https://example.com/%E3%81%93...`, `https://localhost/api?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com`, `https://example.com/%hello` must be unchanged.
3. Keep the existing multibyte `encodeURI` branch. Encode CR/LF after that so both branches are covered (note `encodeURI` already converts CR/LF, so the post-pass is idempotent for the multibyte branch).
4. Keep the return type/signature unchanged.

Tests to add in `src/context.test.ts` near the existing redirect tests (after the `unchangedURLString` block around line 130), covering:
- Raw CR/LF: e.g. `c.redirect('/destination\r\nSet-Cookie: evil=1')` → Location is `/destination%0D%0ASet-Cookie: evil=1` and the response does not contain a `Set-Cookie` injected header.
- Raw LF only and raw CR only, if convenient.
- Percent-encoded input: e.g. `c.redirect('/destination%0D%0ASet-Cookie:...')` stays exactly `%0D%0A` (not double-encoded `%250D%250A`).
- Also assert the response status remains 302.

Run `pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts` from the repo root and report the exact pass/fail summary. Do not modify any files other than `src/context.ts` and `src/context.test.ts`. Do not run git add/commit. Report the final diff (file:line) and test output.

## Summary

Fixed CR/LF header injection in `c.redirect()` without double-encoding valid/percent-encoded locations, and added four regression tests.

### Changes

**`src/context.ts:772-783`** — compute the existing multibyte/verbatim branch first, then escape CR/LF as a post-pass (idempotent for the `encodeURI` branch, since it already emits `%0D`/`%0A`):

```ts
const locationString = String(location)
const encodedLocation =
  // Multibytes should be encoded
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex

  'Location',
  // CR and LF must be encoded to prevent header injection (response splitting).
  // `encodeURI` already encodes them, so this is idempotent for the multibyte branch.
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
  encodedLocation.replace(/[\r\n]/g, (char) => (char === '\r' ? '%0D' : '%0A'))
)
return this.newResponse(null, status ?? 302) as any
```

Signature/return type unchanged. `\r\n` becomes `%0D%0A`, `\n` → `%0A`, `\r` → `%0D`. Already-encoded input like `%0D%0A` is untouched (no `encodeURI` call on the ASCII branch), and valid/multibyte/URL inputs keep their previous behavior.

- `context.test.ts:146` CR-only → `%0D`, status 302, no `Set-Cookie`

part.text:
## Summary

Fixed the CRLF header-injection risk in `c.redirect()` and added regression coverage. All changes are unstaged.

### Implementation — `src/context.ts:772-783`
The location is first passed through the existing multibyte logic, then raw CR/LF are escaped in a post-pass:

```ts
const encodedLocation =
  !/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString) ? locationString : encodeURI(locationString)
this.header(
  'Location',
  encodedLocation.replace(/[\r\n]/g, (char) => (char === '\r' ? '%0D' : '%0A'))
)
```

Why this shape:
- Raw `\r` → `%0D`, `\n` → `%0A`; `\r\n` → `%0D%0A`, so no raw line terminators reach the header.
- Valid ASCII redirects (`/destination`, `https://…`, `URL` objects) pass through unchanged.
- Already percent-encoded input (`%0D%0A`, `%20`, invalid `%hello`) is **not** double-encoded — `encodeURI` is still only applied on the multibyte branch, so `%0D%0A` stays `%0D%0A` (not `%250D%250A`).
- Multibyte behavior is unchanged; `encodeURI` already emits `%0D`/`%0A`, making the post-pass idempotent.
- Signature and return type are untouched.

### Tests — `src/context.test.ts:132-158`
Four regressions covering raw CRLF, LF-only, CR-only, and pre-encoded CRLF:
- Exact `Location` assertions (`%0D%0A` / `%0A` / `%0D`, and unchanged `%0D%0A`).
- Status stays `302`.
- `Location` contains no raw CR/LF.

Per review, the initially-added `Set-Cookie`-is-null checks were removed as vacuous (a `Headers` set can't materialize a second header) and replaced with the direct no-raw-CRLF assertion.

### Verification
```
pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  67 passed (67)
```
Existing redirect tests (`/destination`, URL object, multibyte, percent-encoded variants) all still pass.

### Notes (non-blocking, out of stated scope)
- Other control characters such as NUL (`\x00`) and NEL (`\u0085`) are not escaped; NEL is not an HTTP line delimiter and NUL alone can't inject a header, but hardening those is a possible follow-up.
- Mixed multibyte + percent-encoded targets still get `encodeURI`'d as a whole (pre-existing behavior, e.g. `%20` → `%2520`); unchanged by this fix.
- `src/context.ts:779-782` keeps the explanatory comment inside the argument list; style-only.
